risks.note: The imposition of reciprocal tariffs by the United States - one of the largest markets for textile exports - in April, followed by a further increase in August, led to substantial disruptions in textile exports and adversely impacted the industry.

The West Asia Crisis lifted global crude oil prices, sharply raising synthetic fibre prices and the prices of dyes, chemicals, packing materials and fuel; yarn manufacturers were able to pass on only a part of this abnormal increase to consumers, compressing margins.
risks.risk: Crude-linked input cost inflation with only partial pass-through

risks.note: Demand for synthetic yarn remained subdued through the year, cutting Textile Division production to 3,790 MT from 4,065 MT; management states the outlook for the synthetic value chain in the current year remains challenging owing to persistent subdued demand.
risks.risk: Subdued end-demand in the synthetic value chain

risks.note: Management explicitly flags that ongoing geopolitical situations - the West Asia Crisis and the outbreak of the war in Iran - create volatility and uncertainty in global trade that may adversely impact the Divisions' performance.
risks.risk: Geopolitical volatility and uncertainty in global trade

risks.note: Indian tea production rose about 5% to 1,370 million kgs, improving supply and pulling average auction prices in North India down by around Rs. 22 per kg; the Division's realisation fell by Rs. 13 per kg despite its quality focus, showing the segment's exposure to an industry-wide price cycle it does not control.
risks.risk: Tea price deflation driven by supply

risks.note: The Division's order flow rests on ongoing expansion and upgradation initiatives of a concentrated set of large steel, infrastructure and industrial groups (Reliance Industries, JSW, Tata Steel, ArcelorMittal Nippon Steel, Vedanta, Adani Group, SAIL, RINL, Jindal Stainless, Jindal Ferrous), so a pause in that investment cycle would directly hit the Division.
risks.risk: Dependence of the Engineering (MICCO) Division on the steel-sector capex cycle

risks.note: The Property Division operates against what management describes as challenging market conditions in the commercial real estate sector; its revenue depends on sustaining occupancy and renewing tenancies at enhanced rental rates.
risks.risk: Challenging commercial real estate market conditions

risks.note: Tea and macadamia output at the Malawi step-down subsidiary NTEL both declined year on year (tea 1.71 million kgs from 1.75 million kgs; macadamia 2.15 million kgs from 2.23 million kgs), and the direct Mauritius subsidiary remained loss-making at the pre-tax level with no significant operational activity.
risks.risk: Agricultural / overseas operating exposure in the tea business
